messages:
mika: Quick heads-up — ran a mixed-precision profiling pass on the 13B benchmark w/ dynamic batching + KV cache warmup. Found a nasty perf cliff when switching kernels mid-token at seq len ~512.
ravi: Can you paste the flamegraph/snippet?
mika: Here are the quick profiler notes:
```
profiler: run_id=rp-bleed
avg_token_latency_ms: 12.8 -> 18.5
hotpath: matmul_fp8_kernel -> matmul_int8_k_split
kv_hit_rate: 86% -> 84%
batch_size_dist: dynamic 1-8, 95th=6
mem_copy_spike: +26% during swap
```
jess: hmm swapping kernels mid-request is expected overhead but +44% is big. Is this tied to calibration quant scale changes?
mika: we suspect a mismatch: per-channel scales for weights vs the per-tensor scales the fused kernels expect. When mismatch occurs runtime falls back to a generic INT8 path with different tiling and extra copies.
oliver: did you repro with per-tensor-only calibration? last run was mixed: per-channel convs + per-tensor linears.
mika: per-tensor-only reduced the latency cliff but increased generation divergence on some prompts (token-level KL jump, ~3% affected samples).
anna: what about trimming outliers in the calibration set? we tried percentile-clip at 99.5 — didn’t help latency much but improved worst-case token diffs.
ravi: propose two mitigations: (1) kernel-selector heuristic to avoid swapping kernels inside a request unless predicted latency win > X_ms, (2) jittered KV warmup window so cache isn't repeatedly cold when a swapping event happens.
jess: +1. Also surface per-route calibration policy in console so latency-sensitive routes can pin per-tensor.
mika: another datapoint: binder metrics show memcopy dominates for small batches when mixed kernels are used — copy + rearrange cost > matmul delta.
sre-bot: deploy-1234: rolling canary started on prod-dedicated-1 (10% traffic). Monitor token_latency_ms and kv_hit_rate.
oliver: can we run an A/B: route A uses per-channel, route B per-tensor + percentile clipping (99.5), run 6h and compare 95/99 latencies + quality eval on a held prompt-set?
anna: I'll prepare sampling seeds. Proposed slices: 
- long_tail_dialogs (focus on long sequences, dialogues)
- narrative_code_mix (doc + code style mixed)
Both will exclude the top 0.05% longest sequences (outlier clip).
mika: note the sampler must keep punctuation/token distribution — we saw regressions tied to shifted token distribution (more punctuation -> different kv reuse patterns).
ravi: add to runbook: when calibration triggers fallback, emit `kernel_swap=true` with weight-scale histogram + batch-size histogram in the trace.
jess: I'll open a follow-up PR for kernel-selector heuristic and the per-route override UI. small change, tagging reviewers @oliver @mika.
mika: if we can avoid intra-request kernel swaps we may salvage most perf while keeping per-channel quality gains elsewhere.
oliver: +1. after the A/B let's reconvene tomorrow 10:00am.
anna: noted. kicking off sample gen and a short perf job now.
mika: thanks all :thumbsup:
